name: Epilogue
tagline: Day 30. The hearing. The house. What it's for.
notes: Plays after Lukey's arc is finished (and podcast ep4). Shows the Day 30 hearing, then the final house choice (sets flag.house_choice: 1 = sell, 2 = stay, 3 = demolish), then the matching epilogue for Lukey's ending.

lines: *The house isn't finished yet. Somewhere behind the walls, something is still dripping. And humming Bon Jovi.*
*Day 30. City Hall. The condemnation hearing takes four minutes.*
*Inspector Dan stands up, clears his throat and tells the council that 12 Heartbreak Lane is 'as dry as my sense of humor.' Nobody laughs. The order is lifted anyway.*
*In the back row, Mrs. Pruitt fires a celebratory crossbow bolt into the ceiling. Nobody knows why she's there.*
*That night, you stand alone in the kitchen. It's quiet. It's dry. It's fixed. For real.*
*Day 30. City Hall. The condemnation hearing takes four minutes.*
*Inspector Dan stands up, clears his throat and tells the council that 12 Heartbreak Lane is 'as dry as my sense of humor.' Nobody laughs. The order is lifted anyway.*
*In the back row, Mrs. Pruitt fires a celebratory crossbow bolt into the ceiling. Nobody knows why she's there.*
*That night, you stand in the kitchen. It's quiet. It's dry. And you're not alone: Lukey is sitting on the counter in full shoulder pads, swinging his legs.*
Lukey: So, sweetheart. What are we doing with it?
*The house is fixed. Now you have to decide what it's for.*

choices.text: Sell it. And take Lukey with you.
Sell it to someone who'll love it.
Sell it to someone who'll love it.

Let it go. Some houses have had enough.

lines: *You list the house. At the open house, a lovely woman in her seventies wanders into the kitchen, runs a finger along the sink and says, 'I had a date in a house like this once. He was very... confident.'*
*Lukey hides in the radiator for six hours.*
*You sell to a young couple with a baby on the way. Lukey cries the whole drive to your new place. Not sad crying. Just a LOT of water. You have to run the wipers on the inside of the car.*
*Three days later, the kitchen tap in your new apartment starts to drip.*
You: Lukey.
Lukey: What? New house. A man's gotta make an entrance.
*You stay. Obviously you stay.*
*The flipper finally has a house she isn't flipping. It has a dry kitchen, a dishwasher that beeps passive-aggressively and a ghost who cooks by yelling at you.*
*Every Friday, Inspector Dan pops round 'just to check the pipes.' Every Friday, his shoes get mysteriously soaked.*
Dan: One of these days I'm going to work out how that happens.
Lukey: No he isn't.
*You let the city have the house. It's had a long, damp life. Lukey agrees, on one condition: you take the sink.*
*You take the sink.*
*It sits in the corner of your new kitchen, connected to nothing, perfectly dry. Lukey naps in it like a cat.*
*The old lot becomes a little park with a drinking fountain that never quite stops dripping.*
Lukey: That's not me.
*It's definitely him.*
*You keep his sweatband in your bedside drawer. It's still, somehow, slightly damp.*
*Every time a tap drips anywhere, you do a tiny Running Man. People have started to notice.*
*The 'FIXED IT MYSELF' message still fogs up on the kitchen window every time you boil the kettle. You never wipe it off.*
*At the open house, a lovely woman in her seventies stops in the kitchen, smiles at the sink and says, 'I had a date in a house like this once. He was very confident.'*
*Then, quieter: 'I hope he's somewhere nice.'*
*You sell to a young couple with a baby on the way. Dan signs it off with a pun nobody laughs at.*
*The kitchen never leaks again. Not once. Which is honestly a little bit sad.*
*The heart-shaped drop on the kitchen floor never dries. You put a little rug around it so nobody steps on it.*
*You and the dishwasher reach an understanding. It's what he would have wanted. Eventually. Grudgingly.*
*The torch he was so rude about lives in the drawer by the sink. You never quite manage to throw it out.*
*You don't sell. You can't. You fixed it too well to give it away.*
*Dan comes to Sunday dinner. He tells terrible puns. Nobody floods his shoes anymore, and he seems to miss it.*
*The house is quiet now. A good quiet. Except, very occasionally, very faintly, from somewhere in the walls: 'Woah-oh, we're halfway there...'*
*You love him enough to let his old haunt go, too.*
*You think he'd get it. Some aerobics routines you just have to end on a big finish.*
*Somewhere, someone is definitely muttering that HE could have done the demolition better. You hold the torch anyway.*
*You let the city have it. It's had a long, damp life.*
*The lot becomes a little park. Dan cuts the ribbon and makes a pun about 'breaking ground.' Mrs. Pruitt fires her crossbow.*
*There's a drinking fountain by the gate. It never stops dripping. Nobody can fix it. Nobody tries very hard.*
